sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Robeson County?
sections.html:
The Robeson County Tax Administrator acts as both county assessor and tax collector. One department lists and values real property, personal property and motor vehicles, collects the tax, maintains land records and mapping, and runs reappraisals.

Inside it are three divisions: assessment, tax collections, and land records and GIS. Customer service and delinquent collections sit under collections, and the mapping side assigns parcel identification numbers used by other county offices.

The department is in Lumberton, and its phone number is 910-671-3060. The county also hosts tools for looking up and paying bills online, and a phone payment line, with a convenience fee applying to card payments.

sections.h2: When did Robeson County last reappraise real property?
sections.html:
The county's most recent reappraisal took effect January 1, 2024. State law requires counties to reappraise real property at least every eight years, and the county page says commissioners were considering a four-year cycle.

Appraisers work from roughly 560 appraisal neighborhoods and a schedule of values built from cost, sales and income data, which the Board of Commissioners adopts. Sales between relatives, gifts and trades are not treated as market sales, and the county says a distressed or highly motivated sale price does not automatically set value.

Between reappraisals, value changes only for new construction, demolition, remodeling, zoning changes or error correction. Real property is permanently listed, so you do not file an annual listing unless you built, demolished or lost a program benefit.

sections.h2: When are Robeson County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in August and become due September 1. The county says to pay by January 5 to avoid interest, and the first charge is 2 percent on January 6.

Robeson County property tax billing steps as the county prints them
StepWhat the county says
Bills mailedAugust
Due dateSeptember 1
Pay without interestBy January 5
First interest2% on January 6
After thatThree-fourths of 1% on the first of each month
AdvertisingMarch, with an advertising fee added

State law, G.S. 105-360, sets the same September 1 due date and interest steps. Enforced collection may begin once a bill is delinquent and can include wage garnishment, bank attachment, foreclosure and income tax refund set-off.

sections.h2: How do you list personal property in Robeson County?
sections.html:
Personal property must be listed every year, and the deadline is January 31 to avoid a 10 percent late listing penalty. An extension to April 15 can be granted on written request postmarked by January 31.

  • Individual personal property includes boats, motors, jet skis, mobile homes, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles.
  • Business personal property includes machinery, equipment, computers, furniture, fixtures, supplies and farm machinery.
  • Ownership on January 1 is what triggers the duty to list.

If you listed last year, a form is mailed to your address of record. If none arrives, getting one is your responsibility, so call the tax office.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Robeson County assessment?
sections.html:
Appeals must be postmarked before the Board adjourns, which the county says is typically in late April and advertised before its first meeting. You get an appeal form by making a written request to the Tax Administrator at the Administration Center in Lumberton.

The state calendar sets limits for the board: it first meets no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May under G.S. 105-322. If you disagree with its decision, notice of appeal to the Property Tax Commission is due within 30 days after the board mails its decision, per G.S. 105-290.

The county suggests gathering supporting records such as a purchase price or damage documentation. Confirm the date printed on your own notice.

sections.h2: What tax relief programs does Robeson County offer?
sections.html:
North Carolina has three relief paths, and an owner may use only one. Applications go to the county tax assessor on Form AV-9, should be filed during the January listing period, and are accepted through June 1 before the tax year.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value of a permanent residence, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, within the income limit. NCDOR prints $38,800 for the 2026 tax year.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: taxes capped at 4 percent of income up to the limit and 5 percent above it up to 150 percent, which NCDOR prints as $58,200 for 2026. Excess tax is deferred, and it needs an annual application and five years of ownership and occupancy.

Present use valuation for farm and forest land is a deferment, not an exemption, with back taxes for the current and three prior years if the land leaves the program. Historic property designated by local ordinance is taxed at 50 percent of appraised value. The county veterans office can help with the NCDVA-9 certification at 910-671-3071.

sections.h2: How are Robeson County property taxes handled when you sell?
sections.html:
Ownership is fixed as of January 1, and a sale during the year does not remove the seller's liability. Proration between buyer and seller is a private contract, and the seller receives the bill for the year of transfer.

To ensure nothing is left owing, ask to pay the collector at closing. If the current bill is not yet due, the county takes a prepayment using the prior year's rate. A tax certification is also needed before the deed is recorded at the register of deeds.

Ask the tax office for the current rate. This page does not state one.

faqs.q: When are Robeson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. Bills go out in August, and the county says to pay by January 5 to avoid interest, which starts at 2 percent on January 6.

faqs.q: When was the last Robeson County reappraisal?
faqs.a: It took effect January 1, 2024. State law requires reappraisal at least every eight years, and the county has said commissioners were weighing a four-year cycle.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax when a Robeson County house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: Ownership on January 1 sets liability, and the seller receives the bill for the year of sale. Buyer and seller usually prorate it at closing.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the elderly, disabled or veteran exclusion in Robeson County?
faqs.a: File Form AV-9 with the Tax Administration office, with NCDVA-9 for veterans. Applications should come in during the listing period and are accepted through June 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Robeson County valuation?
faqs.a: The appeal must be postmarked before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, typically late April. Request a form in writing from the Tax Administrator.
